fixtures.title: All four observations stay in the denominator
steps: Against a 1% target, squared shortfalls are 16, 0, 0 and 0 in percentage-point units.
Downside deviation = sqrt(16 / 4) = 2 points; Sortino = (3 − 1) / 2.
fixtures.answer: Monthly period Sortino is 1.0000, with downside deviation of 2 percentage points.

fixtures.title: Known statistics reproduce the series result
steps: Use arithmetic mean 3%, target 1% and matching-period downside deviation 2 points.
Divide the 2-point mean-minus-target return by 2-point downside deviation.
fixtures.answer: The same monthly period ratio is 1.0000; ordinary standard deviation would be a different denominator.

fixtures.title: Changing only the target changes the downside set
steps: Keep the four returns and lower the fixed monthly target from 1% to 0%.
Only the −3% return is below target: downside deviation = sqrt(9 / 4) = 1.5 points.
Mean-minus-target is 3 points.
fixtures.answer: Monthly Sortino becomes 2.0000, rather than 1.0000. The comparison changed its objective.

fixtures.title: Negative mean return keeps a negative ratio
steps: The arithmetic mean is −1%.
Squared shortfalls sum to 10; divide by all four observations before taking the square root.
Sortino = −1 / sqrt(2.5).
fixtures.answer: Period Sortino is about −0.6325, with downside deviation about 1.5811 percentage points.

fixtures.title: Every return meets the target
steps: Each return meets or exceeds the fixed 1% target.
Every shortfall is zero, so downside deviation is zero.
fixtures.answer: The ratio is undefined; it is not reported as infinity, a real zero or a guaranteed good score.

fixtures.title: Annual observations retain their own period
A full loss is accepted as a simple return
Zero entered downside deviation
Monthly rent becomes annual rent before division
steps: Annual gross rent = $2,400 × 12 = $28,800.
Gross annual rent yield = $28,800 / $360,000 × 100 = 8%.
fixtures.answer: The property is priced at 12.5 times scheduled annual rent, with an 8% gross rent yield before expenses.

fixtures.title: Annual and monthly inputs reconcile
steps: Enter $28,800 annual rent instead of $2,400 monthly rent.
The annual rent denominator stays $28,800.
fixtures.answer: GRM remains 12.5 and gross annual rent yield remains 8%. Changing units alone without converting rent would give a wrong comparison.

fixtures.title: Reverse the formula for a selected price
steps: Annualize $2,400 monthly gross rent to $28,800.
Multiply that rent by the user-selected GRM of 12.5.
fixtures.answer: The implied price is $360,000 under that chosen multiplier; this does not verify market value.

fixtures.title: Reverse the formula for required rent
steps: Divide the entered $360,000 price by a selected GRM of 12.5.
Divide $28,800 required annual rent by 12.
fixtures.answer: Required monthly gross rent is $2,400; the calculation does not establish that a tenant will pay it.

Selected liabilities / (liabilities + equity) = 240,000 / 400,000.
fixtures.answer: D/E is 1.5000 and the selected numerator/capital share is 60%.

fixtures.title: A narrower debt definition gives a different ratio
steps: For the same company and $160,000 equity, select $160,000 interest-bearing debt rather than $240,000 total liabilities.
The selected capital denominator is 160,000 + 160,000, excluding $80,000 other liabilities.
fixtures.answer: Borrowing-based D/E is 1.0000 and selected debt/capital is 50%; debt/total assets would instead be 40% if assets are $400,000.

fixtures.title: Repayment and new equity affect different balances
steps: Repay $40,000 from existing company cash: liabilities fall to $200,000 and equity stays $160,000.
Separately raise $40,000 new equity retained as cash: equity becomes $200,000.
Apply both independent entries: D/E = 200,000 / 200,000.
fixtures.answer: D/E moves from 1.5000 to 1.0000; repayment alone gives 1.2500 and new equity alone gives 1.2000.

fixtures.title: New equity can restore a positive denominator
steps: The initial $−20,000 book equity does not receive a meaningful D/E score.
A $70,000 new equity injection retained in the company increases equity to $50,000.
Debt remains $100,000, giving an after-change ratio of 2.
fixtures.answer: The before-change ratio stays flagged. After-change D/E is 2.0000 once equity becomes positive.
